nodes.description: Public mapping (address => uint) that stores the deposited ETH balance of every hodler.
Constant uint partyTime = 1844690399 acting as the release gate for withdrawals.
Anonymous payable fallback function that credits msg.value to the caller's balance and emits Hodl.
Withdraw function requiring block.timestamp > partyTime, zeroing the balance and transferring it out.
Caller-controlled address used as mapping key for deposits/withdrawals and as ETH transfer recipient.
Miner-influenceable timestamp compared against partyTime in the party() require statement.
Unchecked uint addition that mutates hodlers[msg.sender] in the fallback, allowing arithmetic overflow.
External ETH transfer to the untrusted caller after zeroing the stored balance.
Local copy of hodlers[msg.sender] captured before the balance is zeroed and then transferred.

edges.reason: The payable fallback executes the unchecked hodlers[msg.sender] += msg.value update.
msg.sender indexes the hodlers mapping whose balance is incremented without overflow checks.
State variable hodlers is written by the unchecked addition, so its value can overflow.
hodlers[msg.sender] is read into the local variable value inside party().
msg.sender is the untrusted key used to read the balance into local value.
The local value is passed as the amount of the external transfer.
msg.sender is the untrusted recipient of the external ETH transfer, enabling callback-based reentrancy.
The balance write (arithmetic operation) precedes the transfer, so the CEI ordering governs reentrancy risk.
block.timestamp is the miner-influenceable condition that gates execution of party().
The partyTime constant is compared against block.timestamp to authorize withdrawal in party().

normalization_plan.reason: The local variable value is only a temporary carrier of hodlers[msg.sender] and is consumed directly by the external transfer operation, so it can be merged into that core unsafe operation.
